speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are an 8-year-old waking up frightened during sleep; can you describe exactly what you see or hear during these scary episodes?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds very distressing. Do you notice any sudden movements, leg jerking, or a change in heart rate when she wakes up? Also, does she ever seem to be running in place or having a conversation while asleep that she doesn't remember?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Difficulty sleeping with episodes of waking up frightened. I also have Yelling and crying during sleep episodes, Temporary post-episode tiredness, Recollection of bad dreams, Bedtime procrastination.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Nightmare Disorder. The history of recurrent frightening dreams causing awakening, distress, and recall of the dream content, without significant confusion or complex sleep behaviors like sleepwalking, is classic for this condition in an 8-year-old.
